titleTr: Resmi ve gayriresmi dil: müdüre e-posta

explainTr: Aynı fikir, kime yazdığına göre farklı söylenir. Arkadaşına 'Can you send me the form?' dersin; müdüre 'Could you please send me the form?' ya da 'I would be grateful if you could send me the form.' yazarsın. Buna 'register' (dil kayıt düzeyi) denir.
Resmi dilde kısaltma (don't, I'm) kullanmazsın; 'Hi' yerine 'Dear Ms. Carter,' ile başlarsın, 'Thanks' yerine 'Thank you for your time' yazarsın. Kapanış: 'Sincerely,' ya da 'Best regards,'.

Resmi dilde phrasal verb yerine genelde daha ciddi tek kelime seçilir: ask for → request, find out → discover, get → receive, look into → investigate, tell → inform. Mesajın kime gittiğini düşün, sonra tonu seç.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'siz' ve 'sen' ayrımı ile saygı belirtirsin. İngilizcede 'you' tektir; saygıyı kelime seçimi, 'could/would' gibi yumuşatıcılar ve kısaltma kullanmamakla gösterirsin.

reading.title: Hafsa learns about register
reading.text:
Hafsa had a good reason to be nervous on Monday morning. She wanted to write her first email to Dr. Alvarez, the principal of Lincoln Elementary, and she wanted every word to be right.

At first she typed what she would say to a neighbor: "Hi Dr. Alvarez! I'm Hafsa. I wanna work as a sub at your school. Can you tell me what I gotta do? Thanks!" She read it twice and frowned. It felt friendly, but she was not sure it sounded professional.

She showed the draft to Mr. Brown, the school secretary, when she dropped by the front office. He smiled kindly. "Your idea is clear, Hafsa," he said, "but the tone is a little too relaxed for a principal. In English, we change our language depending on the reader. This is called register."

Together they rewrote the message. "Hi" became "Dear Dr. Alvarez," and "I wanna" became "I would like to." The sentence "Can you tell me what I gotta do?" turned into "Could you please inform me of the necessary steps?" Mr. Brown also suggested replacing "Thanks!" with "Thank you for your time and consideration." Finally, he added a closing: "Sincerely, Hafsa Yilmaz."

"Is it too stiff now?" Hafsa asked. "Not at all," he answered. "Formal does not mean cold. It means respectful. You can still sound like yourself. Just avoid slang and contractions in the first message. Once you know someone better, you can relax a bit."

Hafsa copied the new version and added her phone number below her name. Before she clicked send, she read it one more time aloud, slowly. The message now sounded calm and confident, the way she hoped to sound in the classroom.

Two days later, Dr. Alvarez replied: "Dear Ms. Yilmaz, thank you for your message. Please stop by on Thursday at ten." Hafsa smiled. A small change in register had opened a big door.

questions.q: Why did Hafsa frown at her first draft?
options: It sounded friendly but not professional.

questions.q: What can we infer from the end of the story?
options: The formal email made a good impression.
Dr. Alvarez refused to meet Hafsa.
Hafsa decided never to write emails again.
Mr. Brown wrote to the principal himself.
questions.whyTr: Müdür kibarca cevap verip Hafsa'yı davet etti.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Mr. Brown, do you have a minute? I wrote a message to the district office about training days.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Of course. Let me see it. Hmm, the first line says, 'Hey, I need some info about the training.'

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: It is understandable, but a bit casual. Try, 'I am writing to inquire about the upcoming training sessions.'

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I see. 'Inquire' is more formal than 'ask,' right?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Exactly. And instead of 'Can you send me the dates,' you could write, 'Could you please send me the dates?'

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: That sounds more polite. What about the ending? I wrote, 'Thanks a lot, see you soon.'

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: For a district office, I would write, 'Thank you for your assistance. Sincerely, Hafsa Yilmaz.'

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: And should I use contractions like 'I'm' or 'don't'?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: It is safer to write them out in the first message. 'I am' and 'do not' look more careful.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Thank you. I will fix it today and send it before lunch.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Good. If you want, bring it back and I will take one more look.

writing.promptTr: Müdür Dr. Alvarez'e resmi bir e-posta yaz: okulda gönüllü olarak çalışmak istiyorsun ve bir görüşme talep ediyorsun. 120-180 kelime.
writing.promptEn: Write a formal email to the principal, Dr. Alvarez. Explain that you would like to volunteer at the school and request a meeting. Write 120-180 words.
frames: I am writing to inquire about ...
Thank you for your time and consideration.
writing.model:
Dear Dr. Alvarez,

My name is Hafsa Yilmaz, and I recently moved to Springfield from Turkey. I am writing to inquire about volunteer opportunities at Lincoln Elementary School. I have two years of experience helping children with reading at a community center, and I would like to continue that work in a school.

I would also like to request a short meeting with you to discuss how I could assist teachers. Would Thursday morning be convenient? If that day is not suitable, I am happy to adapt to your schedule. I have enclosed a copy of my resume for your review. I would appreciate it if you could confirm a time at your earliest convenience.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Hafsa Yilmaz
checklistTr: En az iki resmi kalıp (I would like to, I am writing to, would appreciate) var mı?
